results.title: How Confirmation Bias Affects your Analysis
results.content: Published Time: 2023-04-10 10:39:32 -0700 How Confirmation Bias Affects your Analysis * Increase Ecommerce Sales with Metrics _Last modified: December 19, 2019_ Confirmation bias is the tendency to **seek out or interpret data to confirm beliefs you already hold**. In a business context, this means ignoring data that is suggesting that some aspect of your feature, product, or business is not working because you found another metric that seems to suggest that it is working. Confirmation bias pressures you to ignore the negative signs and focus on the positive. How to Detect Confirmation Bias? There are three common signs that confirmation bias is influencing the data you are looking at. ### Only good news If the only news is good news confirmation bias is probably hiding some inconvenient metrics. If people are confidently sharing convoluted proxy metrics, they are likely looking for ways to find positive signals in the data. What to do about Confirmation Bias? ### Institutionalized disconfirmation Institutionalized disconfirmation is how academia addresses the confirmation bias problem. Reproducibility is a much higher bar than examining the analysis, it provides more data to confirm what the paper has laid out. **How can you apply this to your company?** The first step is to create a peer review process. Before an analysis is presented to the company have a system in place where another analyst reviews your analysis to see if they reach the same conclusions. If you have the time and resources it may be worth trying to replicate a test run within your company to confirm its findings. ### 3rd party audit Hiring a 3rd party audit is how government tends to address the confirmation bias problem. **How can you apply this practice to your company?** Use data analysts to randomly check analysis being shared. ### Insurance rules This is one way business tries to address the confirmation bias problem. It does not prevent confirmation bias so much as it places rules on the company to prevent certain errors from happening. **How can you apply this practice to your company?** Create parameters of what people can and can’t claim with their data. ### Culture This is another way businesses try to address the confirmation bias problem.

results.content: Home > Attention > Naïve Realism: Our Misinterpretation of How We Interpret the World. The act of engaging in top-down processing leaves us vulnerable to naïve realism because it can result in a biased opinion. A previous blog post discusses how naïve realism can lead to the blind spot bias and being overly self-confident. The passage on naïve realism explained how it can negatively impact people by maintaining fixed viewpoints and rejecting other opinions. Thus, it seems that top-down processing is a double-edged sword within the context of naïve realism. But, if we consciously access knowledge about naïve realism, we can work to reduce the bias. Overcoming the barrier of narrative adherence in conflicts through awareness of the psychological bias of naïve realism. Addressing your first question, yes, even just the knowledge of naïve realism can lead to the reduction of bias. Also, I would assume that external knowledge can help reduce naïve realism. It seems like naïve realism has some degree of overlap with confirmation bias, or the phenomenon in which one only seeks out and regards facts and opinions that validate their own beliefs. In a case like this, someone who has read both your post and one about confirmation bias will be able to recognize that this naïve realism arose from the person only considering the information that’s in agreement with his or her opinion. Moreover, attention (or lack thereof) would also affect one’s experience with naïve realism and confirmation bias; when one pays more attention to the information that supports his or her beliefs, he/she is more likely to remember it. As you mentioned in your post, naïve realism is dependent on top-down processes, which involve integrating preexisting assumptions and expectations into our cognition. results.title: How to Validate User Feedback and Avoid Confirmation Bias
results.content: # How do you validate product user feedback and avoid confirmation bias? User feedback is a valuable source of insight for product development, but it can also be misleading if not validated properly. How do you validate product user feedback and avoid confirmation bias? To ensure fair validation of user feedback and avoid bias, gather input from a diverse group of users. To validate product user feedback and mitigate confirmation bias, utilize diverse sources of feedback, including surveys, interviews, and user analytics. Ask open-ended questions and use a variety of feedback sources to validate user feedback and prevent confirmation bias. User feedback can come in different forms, such as surveys, interviews, focus groups, usability tests, reviews, ratings, analytics, etc. To validate user feedback, you should use multiple sources and methods that complement each other, and triangulate the data to find patterns, gaps, and discrepancies. The importance of using multiple sources and methods to validate user feedback is unavoidable. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of user feedback can only be achieved by triangulating data from multiple sources. To validate product user feedback and avoid confirmation bias, employ multiple sources and methods. Another way to avoid confirmation bias is to seek diverse and representative samples of users who can provide feedback. The way you ask questions can also influence the quality and validity of user feedback. This approach can greatly enhance the validity of user feedback, leading to more accurate product improvements. Finally, to validate user feedback and avoid confirmation bias, you should challenge and test your assumptions and hypotheses with data and evidence. This means that you should not take user feedback at face value, but rather question its validity, reliability, and relevance. User feedback is great, but test it with data and experiments. By turning feedback into an ongoing conversation, you establish a dynamic connection with your user base, ensuring your product continually aligns with their expectations and business goals. You need to gather user feedback for your product. How do you balance user feedback with your own vision and goals for the product? How do you measure the impact of user feedback on your product outcomes?
